A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GROD study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and identifying the removed NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original image and text OOD-detection experiments, ablations, Gaussian-mixture simulations and feature visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds ImageNet-200 evaluations and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: V1 enables LDA when B/K > 2 and uses eligible classes having multiple batch examples. V2 selects the most populated eligible classes, capped by [2B/(K*num)], and uses whether the selected set I is empty to determine generation and filtering branches. This refines outlier generation while retaining the PCA/LDA framework, Gaussian synthesis, losses and ViM post-processing.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet-200 as an ID benchmark evaluated against CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN. Appendix J.2 identifies it as an ImageNet-1K subset, distinct from the retained Tiny ImageNet dataset. Existing CIFAR, text and Gaussian-mixture coverage remains.

E2.justification: The image comparisons retain MSP, ODIN, ViM, GEN, ASH, G-ODIN, NPOS and CIDER; the text comparisons retain their previous subset. The ImageNet-200 experiment extends the existing comparator set. The newly cited RONF work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces timing evaluation: Figure 2 measures training seconds per image per epoch and test-time seconds per image. Existing backbones, detection metrics, 20-epoch budget, batch size 64 and validation-based checkpoint selection are retained. The PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 2 add an efficiency analysis comparing training and post-processing overhead across image datasets and methods. The hyperparameter and component ablations, Gaussian-mixture investigations, t-SNE visualizations and likelihood analyses are retained without new underlying results.

E5.justification: Both versions report five data-generation seeds for the Gaussian-mixture optimization experiments and display the same means and standard-deviation bands in v1 Figure 4 and v2 Figure 5. No additional uncertainty estimates, run counts or significance tests accompany the main benchmark or timing results.

E6.justification: V2 adds ImageNet-200 scores and timing results. Table 4 reports GROD ID accuracy of 90.71%, average FPR@95 of 18.26% and average AUROC of 95.24%; CIDER has a lower average FPR@95 of 15.97%. V1 Tables 1–4 match v2 Tables 2, 3, 5 and 6 numerically. These are additional results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: V2 introduces the formal selection count n and redefines I as a top-n subset in Section 3, Equations 4–5. Beyond these procedural mathematical definitions, the PAC learnability assumptions, probability definition, theorems, bounds, appendix lemmas and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 removes the abstract’s explicit image and text performance-improvement figures, including the image FPR@95 comparison from 21.97% to 0.12%. The central claims of a novel GROD algorithm, transformer PAC guarantees and strong performance across image and text tasks remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning sufficient ID data, computational efficiency and interference from OOD techniques when the ImageNet-200/SVHN baseline already performs well. It also proposes a future standard for assessing synthetic-outlier quality. Its new blanket superiority and speed statements exceed the mixed evidence in Table 4 and Figure 2.

D1.justification: Appendix J adds parameter-selection guidance, including gamma between 0.1 and 0.3, and identifies the ImageNet-200 subset through OpenOOD. Hardware, default optimization settings and the code link remain unchanged. Revised Algorithm 1 also places model updates inside the optional random-filtering condition, introducing an implementation ambiguity absent from v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds Deng et al. (2009) for ImageNet and He et al. (2022, RONF). Appendix K newly positions GROD as overcoming synthetic outliers’ failure to represent real outliers. The broader related-work discussion is retained; the switch to author-year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain. V2 makes localized method and interpretation revisions, expands parameter guidance, updates author information and removes the NeurIPS checklist. It also introduces awkward 'Eq. equation' references. There is no wholesale narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adds the dataset-summary Table 1, ImageNet-200 Table 4 and two-panel timing Figure 2. It adopts ICLR formatting and relocates retained displays, including placing both final visualizations together. All six original figure artworks are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added ImageNet-200 and timing evidence makes scale and cost tradeoffs more assessable, and removing the abstract’s mislabeled SOTA numbers improves accuracy: those v1 numbers belonged to MSP. However, v2 introduces an unresolved conditional-update problem in Algorithm 1 and overstates comparative performance and speed despite counterexamples in Table 4 and Figure 2. These useful additions coexist with procedural and interpretive defects, preventing a confident net quality judgment from the PDFs.
